props.gloss_en: Rav Menashya: a canopy -- we went over every side of the canopy and found no side of permission

Rami bar Yechezkel teaches: a folded cloak -- one may not make [a tent of it], and if he did he is exempt but it is forbidden; if a string or cord was wound on it, it may be spread ab initio (applied to the canopy at 138a.13)
Rav Menashya: hops in a vineyard -- a [forbidden] mixture
hops -- R' Tarfon says: they are not kilayim in a vineyard
and we hold: whoever is lenient in the Land, the halakha follows him outside the Land
because they are not people of Torah [-- said at 139a.17, 139a.18 and 139b.2 of why the leniency was not sent]
Rav would announce: whoever wants to sow hops in a vineyard, let him sow
Rav Amram Chasida would flog for it
Rav Mesharshiya would give a peruta to a gentile child, and he would sow [hops] for him
[not to a Jewish child, for] he will come to be habituated
[not to a gentile adult, for] he will come to be confused with a Jew
Rav Menashya: a dead person -- neither Jews nor Arameans attend to him, neither on the first Festival day nor on the second
[the same reply, its other half:] Jews do not attend to him even on the second Festival day

there was an incident in the Maon synagogue on a Festival adjoining Shabbat -- and I do not know whether before it or after it -- and they came before R' Yochanan, and he said: let gentiles attend to him
Rava: one who died on the first Festival day -- gentiles attend to him
Rava: on the second Festival day -- Jews attend to him
Rava: and even on the second day of Rosh HaShana
Rava: which is not so for an egg (Steinsaltz: an egg laid on the first day of Rosh HaShana stays forbidden on the second)
